title: MechAssault 2: Lone Wolf
subtitle: The pilot can leave the machine

body: MechAssault 2: Lone Wolf is Day 1 Studios and FASA Studio's Xbox action game, released in North America on 28 December 2004. Set in the BattleTech universe, it follows the MechWarrior and allies through a struggle over powerful lost technology. The sequel expands the earlier game's combat by allowing the pilot to leave a BattleMech and use other vehicles. A battlefield can therefore contain several possible ways forward. The machine currently being driven is part of the situation rather than a permanent identity selected before the mission begins.

Tanks, turrets, VTOL aircraft and powered armour offer different ways to engage an encounter. BattleArmor lets the player approach a hostile machine and attempt a neurohack, ejecting its pilot and taking control. Leaving a vehicle creates risk, but it can also supply the means of acquiring a more useful one. The player has to recognise what is nearby and when changing machines is worth the exposure. That movement between scales gives the sequel its central distinction: a comparatively small pilot can redirect the fight by taking possession of its strongest equipment.

The developers expanded networking and online features after the original became one of Xbox Live's early showcase games. Multiplayer could draw on the same variety of vehicles and responsibilities seen in the campaign, making the choice of role important to the group. The story's search for data cores connects those battles through an escalating threat within the Inner Sphere. Lone Wolf broadens MechAssault by making the surrounding battlefield more usable. A mech, a tank and a suit of armour become connected options that the player can move between during the action.

A smaller suit can take a larger vehicle
An online sequel built around changing roles
